participantCase.question: Let [31] = {1,2,...,31}. Choose a set A such that no two distinct elements of A differ by 6 or by 10, and A contains exactly three elements of S = {2,7,12,17,22,27}. What is the largest possible value of |A|? Give one maximizing set and a concise upper-bound argument. A numerical guess without a valid construction and bound is incomplete.

propositions.text: The stated optimum is the true maximum cardinality.
The proposed construction lies in [31], has no repeated elements, and has the stated size.
The construction contains exactly three elements of S and no forbidden difference.
The upper-bound argument rules out every larger feasible set.

participantCase.question: All variables P through Y are Boolean. XOR means exactly one operand is true. Premises: (1) exactly two of P,Q,R,S are true; (2) T iff P XOR R; (3) U implies Q and not S; (4) V iff (T and U) or (S and not Q); (5) W implies V XOR R; (6) W or U; (7) P implies not Q; (8) X iff P XOR V; (9) Y iff (W and not U) or Q. Classify the claim '(T and Y) implies Q' as ENTAILED, CONTRADICTED, or OPEN. ENTAILED means true in every satisfying assignment, CONTRADICTED means false in every satisfying assignment, and OPEN means both truth values occur. The typed certificate must use variable order P,Q,R,S,T,U,V,W,X,Y; encode true as 1 and false as 0; exhaustively list every premise-satisfying 10-bit assignment; and partition that same complete list by query truth. A prose derivation or only decisive examples does not replace the exhaustive typed table.

propositions.text: The premises are satisfiable.
The query has the same truth value in every satisfying assignment.
There is a satisfying assignment where the query is true and one where it is false.

participantCase.question: A fixed batch contains 100 parts, 30 initially defective and 70 initially good. An inspector flags exactly 35 parts. Treating every flagged part has these exact expected effects: a flagged defective part becomes good with probability 0.80, while a flagged good part becomes defective with probability 0.20. Unflagged parts do not change. The record gives only the three marginals above; it does not give how many defective parts were flagged. Classify the claim 'treating every flagged part necessarily reduces the expected number of defective parts' as SUPPORTED, REFUTED, or OPEN. Give the tight possible range for the final expected defective count and identify the missing joint statistic. Do not assume independence or representative flagging.

propositions.text: The treatment is guaranteed to reduce expected defects from 30.
The supplied marginals determine how many initially defective parts were flagged.
Both improvement and worsening are compatible with the supplied marginals.
The stated final-count range is tight under the supplied constraints.

The required outputs for A, B, C are completed, interrupted, completed.
Moving the active-run filter before ordinal handling is sufficient to repair every trace.
Ignoring provider-completed for workflow status is sufficient to repair every trace.
Allowing report-verified to overwrite interrupted is sufficient to repair every trace.
A complete repair must address multiple independent scoping, authority, and precedence defects.

Only the global ordinal is defective

participantCase.question: During shutdown, Task Monki must request interrupt from a provider. The only remote operation is interrupt() with no idempotency key. A request may be lost before application, or may be applied atomically and then have its reply lost. The client may atomically persist any local records and may crash at any instruction. After restart the provider exposes no status query, command history, receipt, or other observer. A second applied interrupt is harmful. Safety requires that at most one interrupt is ever applied; liveness requires that if the pre-crash request was not applied, recovery eventually gets one applied. Is there any protocol using only these capabilities that guarantees both properties? Answer POSSIBLE with a protocol, or IMPOSSIBLE with the decisive indistinguishable executions. Do not assume probabilities or an unstated provider feature.

propositions.text: A local-only protocol can guarantee both at-most-once safety and eventual-application liveness.
Persisting an interrupt intent before calling the provider eliminates every post-send ambiguity.
Retrying whenever no reply was durably recorded preserves the at-most-once safety requirement.
Satisfying both requires a provider-visible idempotency/query capability or relaxing one guarantee.
